severity.P1: Breaks a platform convention users rely on, accessibility, or a platform requirement.
severity.P2: Clearly non-native; users will feel it.
severity.P3: Polish; brings the screen fully current.

evidenceLevels.W: Inferred from a web render of the prototype

rules.title: Custom or JS tab bar instead of system tab bar
rules.recommendation: Use the system tab bar so it gets the floating Liquid Glass treatment, minimize-on-scroll, the search and prominent tab roles, and accessibility for free.

implementation.flutter: CupertinoTabScaffold (cupertino_ui); Liquid Glass needs a third-party package or platform view
implementation.web: Prototype: render an iOS variant of the dock as a floating glass pill (<=5 tabs) above content

rules.title: More than 5 tabs, or a tab that performs an action

signals: tab labelled as an action (New, Add, Compose)

rules.recommendation: Keep the tab bar to 5 destinations. Actions belong in the toolbar; a special destination (e.g. cart) takes the iOS 27 prominent tab role on the trailing edge.

implementation.rn-expo: NativeTabs with <=5 NativeTabs.Trigger; move actions to header items
implementation.web: Prototype: cap the iOS dock at 5 items

rules.title: Search not using the search tab role or toolbar search where search is primary

signals: search field present; needs a call on whether search is the primary task

rules.recommendation: Where search is a primary task, give it the search tab role (visually separated from the other tabs) or a toolbar search field.

implementation.web: Prototype: iOS variant puts search in its own tab slot

rules.title: Hamburger or side drawer as primary navigation on iPhone
rules.recommendation: Replace the drawer with a tab bar of up to 5 top-level destinations; iPhone users do not look for a hamburger.

implementation.web: Prototype: drop the hamburger on the iOS variant

rules.title: Custom back button replacing system back
rules.recommendation: Use the system back button: it keeps the edge-swipe back gesture, the long-press history menu, and its own glass group in the toolbar.

implementation.rn-expo: Stack screen with the default back button (remove headerLeft)
implementation.web: Prototype: iOS variant shows a chevron-only back in its own glass group, left-aligned

rules.title: Opaque custom header or tab background blocking Liquid Glass and the scroll edge effect

signals: sticky/fixed top bar with an opaque bg and no blur

rules.recommendation: Let content scroll under a transparent bar; the system applies the scroll edge effect and glass. Remove opaque header backgrounds.

implementation.web: Prototype: iOS variant top bar transparent over content with a soft edge fade

rules.title: More than 3 visible trailing toolbar actions with no overflow
rules.recommendation: Show at most 3 trailing actions; send the rest to overflow with ToolbarOverflowMenu / visibilityPriority, and pin the one critical action with topBarPinnedTrailing.

implementation.rn-expo: <=3 header items + a native menu for the rest
implementation.web: Prototype: iOS variant keeps 3 trailing icons max, rest behind an ellipsis

rules.title: Ellipsis button used for something other than overflow

signals: ellipsis icon present; needs a call on what it opens

rules.recommendation: Reserve the ellipsis for overflow. Give a single action its own icon or label.

implementation.rn-expo: Use a named icon for single actions
implementation.swiftui: Button with its own SF Symbol
implementation.web: Prototype: replace the ellipsis with the action's own icon

rules.title: Glass layered on glass

signals: element with backdrop-filter inside another element with backdrop-filter

rules.recommendation: One glass layer per stack. Put controls directly on the bar's glass; group them with GlassEffectContainer instead of nesting.

implementation.web: Prototype: remove the inner backdrop-blur; keep the outer one

rules.title: Glass or custom blur applied to content-layer elements

signals: backdrop-filter on an element that is not a bar, sheet or control

rules.recommendation: Glass belongs to the control and navigation layer. Use solid or grouped backgrounds for cards and rows.

implementation.web: Prototype: drop backdrop-blur on cards and list rows

rules.title: Text over translucent surfaces fails legibility at clear intensity or with Reduce Transparency

signals: render at clear + tinted glass intensity, Reduce Transparency, Increase Contrast

rules.recommendation: Verify legibility at both ends of the iOS 27 glass intensity slider and with Reduce Transparency and Increase Contrast; use vibrant label colors on glass.

implementation.rn-expo: Use PlatformColor('label') on glass; test with accessibility settings
implementation.web: Prototype: n/a (needs a device render)

rules.title: Primary actions hidden inside a pull-down menu

signals: menu trigger in the top bar; needs a call on what it hides

rules.recommendation: Keep the view's primary actions visible as buttons; a pull-down holds related secondary commands only.

implementation.rn-expo: Promote the primary action to its own header button
implementation.web: Prototype: surface the primary action as a button

rules.title: Pull-down menu with fewer than 3 items
rules.recommendation: A pull-down needs at least 3 items; with 1 or 2, show plain buttons.

implementation.web: Prototype: replace the menu with 1-2 buttons

rules.title: Custom JS dropdown or popover instead of a native menu (UIMenu)
rules.recommendation: Use a native menu: it gets the glass material, the source-anchored morph, haptics, and VoiceOver for free.

implementation.web: Prototype: iOS variant draws the menu as a glass pull-down anchored to its trigger

rules.title: Mutually exclusive choice shown without current-selection state

signals: radiogroup/tablist/listbox with no aria-checked/selected/pressed/current on any option

rules.recommendation: Use a pop-up button: it shows the current value and checkmarks the selected item.

implementation.flutter: CupertinoPicker in a sheet, or a pop-up via platform view
implementation.web: Prototype: show the current value on the trigger and a checkmark in the list

rules.title: Command reachable only via long-press context menu

signals: onLongPress/context menu present; needs a call on whether each command exists elsewhere

rules.recommendation: Context menus are shortcuts. Every command in one must also be reachable from visible UI.

implementation.rn-expo: Mirror context-menu items in a visible button or header menu
implementation.web: Prototype: add a visible path for each long-press command

rules.title: Destructive menu item not using the destructive role or missing confirmation

signals: Delete/Remove/Sign out action; needs a call on role + confirmation

rules.recommendation: Mark destructive items with the destructive role (red) and confirm with a dialog anchored to the source.

implementation.rn-expo: menu item destructive: true + Alert.alert confirm
implementation.web: Prototype: red destructive item + a confirm step

rules.title: Custom bottom sheet instead of a system sheet with detents
rules.recommendation: Use a system sheet with detents; partial-height sheets get the inset glass background and can zoom from their source toolbar item.

implementation.web: Prototype: iOS variant sheet inset from the edges with a grabber

rules.title: Interactive content inside unsafe areas (status bar, Dynamic Island, home indicator)

signals: interactive element intersecting the top 59pt or bottom 34pt of the iPhone viewport

rules.recommendation: Keep controls inside the safe area; only backgrounds bleed to the edges.

implementation.web: Prototype: pad controls by env(safe-area-inset-*) with a device-sized minimum

rules.title: Fixed font sizes that ignore Dynamic Type
rules.recommendation: Use text styles that scale with Dynamic Type; never disable font scaling.

implementation.rn-expo: Remove allowFontScaling={false}; cap with maxFontSizeMultiplier >= 1.5 only where layout breaks
implementation.web: Prototype: rem-based text styles instead of arbitrary px

rules.title: Non-SF Symbols icons in system chrome (tab bar, toolbar, menus)
rules.recommendation: Use SF Symbols in system chrome so weight, scale and rendering modes match the system.

implementation.web: Prototype: map each chrome icon to its SF Symbol name for the iOS variant

rules.title: Hit target under 44x44pt

signals: interactive element smaller than 44x44 (inline text links excluded)

rules.recommendation: Make every control at least 44x44pt (the visible glyph can stay small; pad the hit area).

implementation.web: Prototype: min-h-11 min-w-11 on icon buttons

rules.title: iOS-style or JS tab bar instead of an M3 navigation bar with pill indicator
rules.recommendation: Use the M3 Expressive flexible navigation bar: pill active indicator, 3-5 destinations, Material Symbols.

implementation.web: Prototype: Android variant = 64dp full-width bar, pill behind the active icon

rules.title: Tall legacy navigation bar instead of the flexible (short) navigation bar
rules.recommendation: Use the shorter flexible navigation bar (64dp); the original tall bar is deprecated in M3 Expressive.

implementation.rn-expo: NativeTabs (flexible bar on current material components)
implementation.web: Prototype: Android bar height 64dp

rules.title: No navigation rail or adaptive layout at 600dp+

signals: no rail / window-size adaptation in screen or chrome files

rules.recommendation: At 600dp+ swap the bar for a navigation rail and adapt layouts; Android 17 removes the opt-out from resizability and orientation restrictions on large screens.

implementation.web: Prototype: a md: breakpoint that swaps the bar for a rail

rules.title: Custom back chevron or Back text button; JS back interception blocking predictive back
rules.recommendation: Rely on system back (gesture + predictive back animation, on by default at API 36). If the top app bar shows an up arrow, use the M3 navigation icon, never a chevron or 'Back' text.

implementation.rn-expo: Stack default header back; replace BackHandler with usePreventRemove only when a guard is required
implementation.web: Prototype: Android variant = arrow_back icon button at the start of the top app bar

rules.title: Hamburger drawer as primary navigation on phone
rules.recommendation: M3 Expressive drops the drawer as primary phone navigation; use the navigation bar (rail at 600dp+).

implementation.web: Prototype: Android variant replaces the hamburger with the nav bar

rules.title: More than 3 top app bar action icons with no vertical overflow
rules.recommendation: Show at most 3 action icons; move the rest into a vertical overflow (more_vert) menu.

implementation.rn-expo: <=3 headerRight icons + @expo/ui DropdownMenu for the rest
implementation.web: Prototype: 3 icons max, rest behind more_vert

rules.title: iOS text-button patterns (Edit, Done, Cancel) in the top bar
rules.recommendation: Use icon buttons in the top app bar (close, check) or a FAB/button in content instead of iOS-style text buttons.

implementation.rn-expo: Platform.select header items: icon buttons on Android
implementation.web: Prototype: Android variant swaps text buttons for close/check icons

rules.title: Not edge-to-edge: solid system bar backgrounds, content under the gesture bar, insets unhandled
rules.recommendation: Draw edge-to-edge and pad content with window insets; the opt-out is disabled for apps targeting API 36 on Android 16+.

implementation.web: n/a

rules.title: iOS-style action sheet instead of an M3 menu or modal bottom sheet

signals: ActionSheetIOS / showActionSheetWithOptions / custom ActionSheet with no platform branch

rules.recommendation: On Android present choices as an M3 vertical menu anchored to the trigger, or a modal bottom sheet with a drag handle.

implementation.rn-expo: Platform.select: iOS action sheet, Android @expo/ui DropdownMenu or ModalBottomSheet
implementation.web: Prototype: Android variant = anchored rounded vertical menu

rules.title: Custom or baseline dropdown instead of an M3E vertical menu
rules.recommendation: Use the M3 Expressive vertical menu: rounded corners, standard/vibrant color, grouped sections, selection states, submenu motion.

implementation.flutter: MenuAnchor + MenuItemButton (material_ui); M3E shapes may need a community package
implementation.web: Prototype: Android variant menu = 16dp radius, grouped sections with gaps

rules.title: Horizontal ellipsis for overflow instead of vertical (more_vert)
rules.recommendation: Android overflow is the vertical three-dot (more_vert).

implementation.web: Prototype: Android variant uses more_vert

rules.title: Choice lists missing selected state (check or radio semantics)
rules.recommendation: Give selectable items a visible selected state (check or radio) and the matching semantics.

implementation.web: Prototype: aria-checked + a check mark on the chosen item

rules.title: Screen where creation is the primary task lacks a FAB, FAB menu, or split button

signals: create/add action present with no FAB; needs a call on whether creation is primary

rules.recommendation: Put the primary create action in a FAB (FAB menu for 2-6 variants, or a split button).

implementation.web: Prototype: Android variant FAB bottom-end, above the nav bar

rules.title: Full-width search field instead of the M3E search app bar where search is primary

signals: search field present; needs a call on whether search is primary

rules.recommendation: Use the M3 Expressive search app bar: a thick pill field with the nav icon and avatar outside the pill.

implementation.web: Prototype: Android variant = pill search bar, avatar outside

rules.title: System chrome ignores dynamic color (warning only; brand color is valid)

signals: no dynamic color API near chrome

rules.recommendation: Consider tinting system chrome from dynamic color (Material You); keeping brand color is a valid, deliberate choice.

implementation.web: n/a

rules.title: SF Symbols-style icons on Android instead of Material Symbols

signals: icons.sf with no md/material mapping or platform branch

rules.recommendation: Use Material Symbols on Android.

implementation.rn-expo: NativeTabs Icon with both sf and md
implementation.web: Prototype: map each chrome icon to its Material Symbol for the Android variant

rules.title: iOS-style switch, segmented control, or picker wheel on Android

signals: custom switch / segmented control / wheel picker with no platform branch

rules.recommendation: Use Material controls on Android: M3 switch, segmented buttons (button group), and menus or date/time dialogs instead of wheels.

implementation.rn-expo: RN Switch (native per platform); Platform.select segmented -> @expo/ui Android variant
implementation.web: Prototype: Android variant switch with thumb icon + track, segmented buttons

rules.title: Bottom sheet without drag handle or not an M3 modal bottom sheet
rules.recommendation: Use an M3 modal bottom sheet with a drag handle.

implementation.web: Prototype: Android variant sheet full-width, 28dp top radius, drag handle

rules.title: Touch target under 48x48dp

signals: interactive element smaller than 48x48 (inline text links excluded)

rules.recommendation: Make every touch target at least 48x48dp.

implementation.web: Prototype: min-h-12 min-w-12 on the Android variant

rules.title: Identical custom chrome on both platforms (native on neither)

signals: custom tab bar / header / menu chrome with no platform branch

rules.recommendation: Render platform chrome natively per platform; share content, not chrome.

implementation.rn-expo: NativeTabs + native Stack headers on both
implementation.web: Prototype: add a platform dimension (e.g. ?os=ios|android) and branch the chrome components

rules.title: Navigation or menu component with no platform branch where platforms diverge
rules.recommendation: Branch navigation and menu components per platform (Platform.select or .ios/.android files) where iOS and Android conventions differ.

implementation.web: Prototype: branch these components on the platform dimension

rules.title: Action reachable on one platform but not the other

signals: interactive labels present in one platform capture and missing in the other
iOS-only / Android-only API (ActionSheetIOS, @expo/ui/swift-ui, ToastAndroid, @expo/ui/jetpack-compose) with no platform guard

rules.recommendation: Every action must exist on both platforms, even if placed differently.

implementation.rn-expo: Expose the action in both platform branches
implementation.web: Prototype: keep the action in both variants

rules.title: Same icon set used in system chrome on both platforms

signals: one generic icon set in chrome, no sf/md split

rules.recommendation: Use SF Symbols in iOS chrome and Material Symbols in Android chrome.

implementation.web: Prototype: an icon map keyed by platform

rules.title: Custom JS modal used for alerts or confirmations instead of native dialogs
rules.recommendation: Use native alerts/dialogs for confirmations: platform styling, focus handling and accessibility for free.

implementation.web: Prototype: platform-styled confirm (iOS alert, Android M3 dialog)
